note: TOWN_LIFE §3.1 (TL-A2): a porter walking with a box or sack on the right shoulder: an upper-body layer on the retail WALK (its legs, feet and root are kept, so its contacts and its 1.17 s cycle are the WALK's own), baked as one clip. The right wrist is solved every frame to hold the load on top of the shoulder (from the upper arm's head: [forward, up, right] metres, turning with the neck: reachFrame; the humeral twist stays 0: twist false, so the folded forearm never rolls); the left arm keeps the WALK's swing (null). The torso leans a little forward and away from the load (side: + leans right); only Spine1 and up move. The load is a socket prop on the right hand (TOWN_LIFE §3.1): its frame-0 spot on top of the shoulder is `origin`, and the hand keeps its rotation relative to the neck (`steady`) so the load does not wobble. Shared by both skeletons.
